description: Verify ARP cache merge on Request followed by gratuitous Response, both from the same IP but different MACs — mixed-stimulus variant of ARP_32/33
approach:
[Objective]
The merge invariant must hold across stimulus shapes. ARP_34 seeds with a Request (MAC-ADDR1) then announces an update with a gratuitous Response (MAC-ADDR2). UDP egress must use MAC-ADDR2.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request (sender_ip=HOST-1-IP, sender_mac=MAC-ADDR1)

2. Tester → DUT: gratuitous ARP Response (sender_ip=HOST-1-IP, sender_mac=MAC-ADDR2)
   ⇒ Cache entry should now be MAC-ADDR2.

3. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup → DUT sends UDP.

4. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: UDP with eth_dst == MAC-ADDR2   ← key check

[Pass condition]
DUT's UDP eth_dst equals MAC-ADDR2.

[Fail condition]
Same as ARP_32 — Fail_used_mac1 / Fail_unknown_mac / Fail_dut_arp_request / Fail_timeout.

verdicts.Pass: DUT used MAC-ADDR2 — Request→Response merge worked
verdicts.Fail_used_mac1: DUT used MAC-ADDR1 — Response did not overwrite Request entry
verdicts.Fail_unknown_mac: DUT used some other MAC — cache corrupt
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not emit UDP within window
